subject: Automotive & EVs
title: The Bugatti Veyron
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Bugatti Veyron.

hook.text: Volkswagen told engineers to build a 1,000-horsepower car that hits 250 mph. They said it was impossible.

buildup.text: The Veyron used a quad-turbo W16 engine—essentially two V8s fused together making 1,001 horsepower.

discovery.text: It hit 253 mph, making it the fastest production car in the world when launched in 2005.

twist.text: VW lost about $6 million on every Veyron sold. It cost $1.5 million but cost far more to build.

climax.text: Just 450 were made. The Veyron proved that no speed barrier is truly impossible with enough engineering.

punchline.text: The Veyron was a money-losing masterpiece.

quiz.question: How much did VW lose on each Veyron?

details.summary: The Bugatti Veyron, launched in 2005, was an engineering marvel with a quad-turbo W16 engine producing 1,001 horsepower, becoming the first production car to exceed 250 miles per hour.
details.whyItMatters: The Veyron proved that automotive engineering could achieve what most experts called impossible. It reset expectations for speed, luxury, and technology in the hypercar world.
takeaways: Its W16 engine uses four turbochargers producing 1,001 HP
Top speed reached 253 mph, then a world record for production cars
Each Veyron reportedly cost Bugatti over 5 million dollars to build

faq.question: Did Bugatti make money on the Veyron?
faq.answer: No. Parent company Volkswagen reportedly lost over 6 million dollars on each car sold. The Veyron was a technology showcase and brand builder rather than a profitable product line.

faq.question: How fast can the Veyron actually go?
faq.answer: The original hit 253 mph. The later Super Sport variant reached 268 mph. A special speed key and a second mode activation are required to unlock full top speed, as the standard mode limits it.
